module_title: Weightages, Baskets, and the RBI Policy Shift
introduction: Both indices are calculated using a specific 'Basket' of items. However, the items inside these baskets are given different 'Weights' (importance). At this level, we will look inside these baskets and understand a historic shift in RBI's policy.

core_concepts.title: Weightage in WPI (Total 697 Items)
core_concepts.description:
The WPI basket is heavily dominated by factory output. 
1. Manufactured Goods: ~64.2% (Highest weight).
2. Primary Articles (food, non-food): ~22.6%.
3. Fuel and Power: ~13.1%.

core_concepts.title: Weightage in CPI
core_concepts.description:
The CPI basket is heavily dominated by survival needs. 
1. Food and Beverages: ~45.8% (Highest weight).
2. Housing, Fuel, Light, Clothing, and Misc (Services): The remaining ~54%.

core_concepts.title: The Urjit Patel Committee Shift (2014)
core_concepts.description: Historically, the RBI used the WPI to measure inflation and set its Repo Rate. However, in 2014, based on the Urjit Patel Committee's recommendation, the RBI officially shifted to using 'CPI-Combined' as its primary inflation anchor. Why? Because WPI does not reflect what the common man actually pays.

core_concepts.title: The Base Effect
core_concepts.description: A mathematical phenomenon often mentioned in news. If inflation was unusually high in August of last year, the inflation rate for August of this year will mathematically look artificially low, simply because it is being compared to an already high base. This optical illusion is called the 'Base Effect'.

important_entities.name: Food Inflation Sensitivity
important_entities.significance: Because 'Food & Beverages' make up almost 46% of the CPI basket, a bad monsoon or a sudden spike in onion/tomato prices will instantly cause CPI inflation to shoot up violently, whereas WPI might remain relatively stable.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: If a question asks: 'Which index does the RBI currently use to target inflation in India?' Do NOT choose WPI. Since 2014, the official answer is strictly 'CPI (Combined)'.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: WPI loves Factories, CPI loves Food
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: WPI Highest Weight = Manufactured Products (64%). CPI Highest Weight = Food & Beverages (46%).

exam_strategy_tips: UPSC frequently tests the conceptual differences in weightages. Remember: A spike in global crude oil prices affects WPI much faster and heavily than CPI, because WPI has a dedicated, higher weight for commercial Fuel and Power.
